question: In My Hero Academia, the freckled green-haired protagonist starts the story without any superpower at all in a world where almost everyone has one. What is his nickname?
context: Izuku Midoriya was bullied by Katsuki Bakugo since childhood; Bakugo coined Deku as an insult meaning 'useless.' Ochaco Uraraka later reframed it as a hero name.

question: In My Hero Academia, the number-one symbol-of-peace hero who passes his power down to Deku is a blond, muscle-bound American-comic-style figure. What's his name?
context: All Might's true form is the gaunt Toshinori Yagi. The power he passes down is called One For All, originally stolen by his master from his villainous brother.

question: The orange-jumpsuit-wearing ninja protagonist of Masashi Kishimoto's 1999 manga has whisker-marks on his cheeks because a nine-tailed fox is sealed inside him. Name him.
context: The Nine-Tails (Kurama) was sealed in baby Naruto by his father, the Fourth Hokage, who died in the sealing. Naruto's dream from page one is to become Hokage himself.

question: Monkey D. Luffy, the straw-hat-wearing protagonist of Eiichiro Oda's pirate epic, gained his stretchy rubber-body powers from eating what kind of magical fruit?
context: Luffy ate the Gomu Gomu no Mi (Gum-Gum Fruit) as a child. Devil Fruit eaters gain a unique power but lose the ability to swim — a major drawback for pirates.

question: In Tite Kubo's Bleach, the orange-haired teenager who becomes a Soul Reaper after meeting Rukia carries a giant sword called a zanpakuto. What's his name?
context: Bleach ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016. Ichigo's zanpakuto, Zangetsu, takes the form of a massive cleaver-style blade in its sealed form.

question: In Hajime no Ippo, the bullied high-school protagonist who discovers boxing after being saved by a pro fighter is a quiet, mop-haired teenager. What's his name?
context: Morikawa Jouji's manga began in 1989 and is still running, making it one of the longest sports manga in history. Ippo's mother runs a fishing-charter business.

question: In Demon Slayer, the gentle protagonist becomes a demon-killer to save his sister Nezuko, who was turned into a demon during a massacre of their family. What's his name?
context: Koyoharu Gotouge's Kimetsu no Yaiba ran from 2016 to 2020 in Weekly Shonen Jump. Tanjiro carries a small wooden box on his back containing his demon sister Nezuko.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's 1988 Studio Ghibli film features two sisters who befriend a giant grey furry forest spirit in rural Japan. What's the title creature's name?
context: My Neighbor Totoro was released as a double feature with Takahata's Grave of the Fireflies. The two sisters Satsuki and Mei live in the countryside while their mother is in the hospital.

question: In the Pokemon anime, the Team Rocket trio chasing Ash consists of a redheaded woman, a blue-haired man, and a talking cat. Name the cat.
context: Meowth taught himself to walk and talk to impress a female Meowth named Meowzie. The Jessie-James-Meowth trio appears in nearly every episode of the original Indigo League series.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball protagonist with a monkey-tail and a power pole carries a four-star orange ball given to him by his grandfather Gohan. What's the boy's name?
context: Goku is a Saiyan from the planet Vegeta, sent to Earth as a baby. Toriyama based Dragon Ball loosely on the Chinese novel Journey to the West, with Goku as the Monkey King Sun Wukong.

question: In Dragon Ball, Goku's signature blue energy-beam attack — formed by cupping the hands at the hip before thrusting them forward — is announced with what shouted name?
context: Goku learns the Kamehameha from Master Roshi after just one demonstration. Master Roshi spent fifty years developing the technique. Yamcha and Krillin also learn it; Vegeta refuses to use it on principle.

question: The famous Death Note manga begins when a Japanese high-schooler picks up a black notebook dropped by a bored shinigami. What is the protagonist's name?
context: Tsugumi Ohba wrote and Takeshi Obata illustrated Death Note from 2003 to 2006. The rules say any human whose name is written in the notebook will die, provided the writer knows their face.

question: In Fullmetal Alchemist, the short alchemist who lost an arm and a leg attempting to bring his mother back from the dead is nicknamed for his prosthetic. What's his nickname?
context: Edward Elric is the youngest State Alchemist in Amestris history, certified at age twelve. His brother Alphonse's soul is bound to a hollow suit of armor after the same failed human transmutation.

question: Naoko Takeuchi's 1991 magical-girl manga features a clumsy schoolgirl who transforms into a sailor-suited heroine alongside friends named after other planets. Who is she?
context: Usagi Tsukino (renamed Serena in the English dub) gets her powers from a talking cat named Luna. The team grew through the series to include Sailors Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and later the outer planets.

question: Demon Slayer's blonde swordsman who falls asleep mid-fight and becomes a deadly Thunder Breathing master while unconscious is a comic-relief teammate of Tanjiro. Name him.
context: Zenitsu can only execute the First Form of Thunder Breathing, but he does it at a speed no one else matches. His ex-grandfather-master Jigoro Kuwajima trained him alongside the demon-turned Kaigaku.

question: Death Note's antagonist detective who eats sweets nonstop, sits in a strange crouch, and is known only by a single letter is Light Yagami's main opponent. What letter?
context: L Lawliet was raised at Watari's orphanage Wammy's House along with his eventual successors Near and Mello. He communicates anonymously through Watari and refuses to show his face in public.

question: In Attack on Titan, the human cities are protected by three concentric giant walls. The innermost, royal-residence wall is named after which queen?
context: Hajime Isayama's manga began in 2009. The walls are named (outer to inner) Maria, Rose, Sina. The Survey Corps wing emblem became one of the most recognizable anime symbols of the 2010s.

question: In One Piece, the swordsman first mate of the Straw Hat pirates fights with three swords at once, including one held in his mouth. What's his name?
context: Zoro's three-sword style is called Santoryu. He carries the white-sheathed Wado Ichimonji, which belonged to his childhood friend Kuina. His lifelong goal is to become the world's greatest swordsman.

question: In Yu Yu Hakusho, the orange-pompadour delinquent protagonist hit by a car in episode one while saving a child returns as a Spirit Detective. Name him.
context: Yoshihiro Togashi's manga ran 1990 to 1994 in Weekly Shonen Jump. Yusuke is sent back to life by Koenma, the toddler son of King Yama, ruler of the Spirit World.

question: In Hunter x Hunter, the spiky-green-haired boy from Whale Island who sets out to find his absent father, a legendary Hunter, is the protagonist. Name him.
context: Yoshihiro Togashi (also Yu Yu Hakusho) began Hunter x Hunter in 1998. The manga is famous for years-long hiatuses due to Togashi's health. Gon's father Ging is one of the strongest Hunters alive.

question: Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun's title spirit haunts the third-stall girls' toilet of the school's old building. What is his actual human name, revealed early in the series?
context: Aida Iro's manga began in 2015. Hanako-kun is one of the Seven Mysteries of Kamome Academy. His twin brother Tsukasa Yugi figures into the deeper plot of why he became a school spirit.

question: In Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, the schoolgirl protagonist who meets Hanako and accidentally becomes his assistant carries a secret about her body that's tied to the Mermaid Mystery. Name her.
context: After making her wish to Hanako, Nene develops fish-scaled legs whenever she gets emotional. The bond contract she makes with Hanako binds them spiritually — neither can fully leave the school.

question: In Initial D, the teenage tofu-delivery driver who races a panda-livery AE86 Trueno down the mountain at night is the unassuming racing prodigy. Name him.
context: Shuichi Shigeno's manga began in 1995. Takumi's father Bunta is the one who really taught him by sending him on tofu deliveries up Mt. Akina from age 13, requiring he not spill a cup of water on the dashboard.

question: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3 protagonist is a Japanese delinquent with a star-shaped birthmark who travels to Egypt to defeat the vampire Dio Brando. Name him.
context: Hirohiko Araki's Stardust Crusaders ran 1989 to 1992. Jotaro's Stand, Star Platinum, is one of the most iconic in the series and shouts a rapid-fire battle cry while throwing a flurry of punches.

question: In Naruto, Team 7's silver-haired jonin sensei who reads suggestive orange-covered novels and keeps one eye permanently covered is the famous Copy Ninja. Name him.
context: Kakashi's covered left eye is a Sharingan transplanted from his dying teammate Obito Uchiha during the Third Ninja War. The orange book he reads is Make-Out Paradise by Jiraiya.

question: Demon Slayer's mask-wearing wild-child swordsman who fights with two jagged blades and was raised by boars in the mountains is the rival-turned-teammate of Tanjiro. Name him.
context: Inosuke wears the head of a wild boar over his own (surprisingly pretty) face. His Beast Breathing style is self-taught and includes finger-fang attacks. His mother was killed by the demon Doma.

question: In My Hero Academia, the explosive, foul-mouthed rival to Deku who can detonate sweat from his palms is the original holder of the title's translated name 'Plus Ultra' attitude. Name him.
context: Bakugo's hero name is Dynamight (later changed from his original suggestion 'King Explosion Murder' which UA rejected). He won the Sports Festival in Season 2 while strapped to a pillar in restraint gear.

question: Demon Slayer's main villain, the original demon and progenitor of all others, is a pale-skinned thousand-year-old creature who fears sunlight above all else. Name him.
context: Muzan was created by a Heian-period doctor's experimental treatment to cure his illness. He spent a thousand years hunting the Blue Spider Lily, the only flower that could grant him immunity to sunlight.

question: Fullmetal Alchemist's tall, hollow-armored younger brother whose soul is bound to a suit of armor speaks gently and loves cats despite his terrifying appearance. Name him.
context: Alphonse's body is preserved in the Gate of Truth, alive but separated from his soul. The blood seal on the inside of the armor's neck is the only thing tying his soul to the metal.

question: Studio Ghibli's 1989 film features a young witch-in-training who flies to a seaside town with her black cat and starts a flying-delivery service. What is the cat's name?
context: Kiki's Delivery Service was Miyazaki's adaptation of Eiko Kadono's children's novel. Tradition holds that all young witches must spend a year on their own training; Kiki picks Koriko, a Stockholm-like city.

question: Kohei Horikoshi began publishing My Hero Academia in Weekly Shonen Jump in July 2014. The series is set at U.A. High School, a hero-training academy in a Tokyo-like city. In the anime adaptation by Studio Bones, what year did the first season air?
context: Horikoshi's earlier short story 'My Hero' from 2008 contained an early version of Deku-as-quirkless protagonist. Studio Bones (Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood, Mob Psycho 100) handled all seasons. The manga concluded in 2024.

question: In My Hero Academia, the dual-natured ice-and-fire-quirked student of Class 1-A has a vertical scar over his left eye from a childhood incident with his abusive father, the number-two hero Endeavor. Name the student.
context: Endeavor (Enji Todoroki) arranged his marriage to Shoto's mother specifically for her ice quirk, planning a child capable of surpassing All Might. The scar came from his mother throwing boiling water at him as a child.

question: In Hajime no Ippo, the brash, charismatic middleweight rookie of Kamogawa Boxing Gym trains in absurd ways — including a famous 'one hour shadowboxing with one arm tied behind the back' regimen. He's Ippo's senior at the gym. Name him.
context: Takamura wins multiple weight classes from junior middleweight to heavyweight by the series's later arcs. The gym's coach Genji Kamogawa is a retired Pacific champion who quit boxing to atone for severely injuring an opponent.

question: In Hajime no Ippo, Ippo's signature finishing technique is a rolling-uppercut combination he develops by watching the heavyweight Bryan Hawk on tape and slowing the footage. The move is named after a real-world 1920s heavyweight world champion. What's it called?
context: Jack Dempsey held the world heavyweight title from 1919 to 1926. His bobbing-and-weaving style made him a perpetual moving target. In Hajime no Ippo, Coach Kamogawa initially refuses to teach Ippo the move directly.

question: Demon Slayer's Mugen Train film, adapted from the manga's Mugen Train arc, became Japan's highest-grossing film of all time in late 2020. The film stars one of the nine Hashira against an Upper Moon demon. Which Hashira gets the lead role?
context: Mugen Train grossed over 40 billion yen, surpassing Spirited Away's 20-year record. The Upper Moon Three demon Akaza is Rengoku's opponent. Ufotable's animation drew international box-office attention to anime films.

question: Demon Slayer's nine elite swordsmen called the Hashira are named for the breathing techniques they master. The pillar of Water Breathing in the current generation is the stoic, half-haori-wearing teal-eyed swordsman who saved Tanjiro and Nezuko in chapter one. Name him.
context: Water Breathing has ten forms, with Eleventh — Dead Calm — invented by Giyu himself. He wears a mismatched haori with half being the geometric pattern of his sister Tsutako's kimono and half his late friend Sabito's.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga ran from 1999 to 2014 in Weekly Shonen Jump. The hidden village Naruto belongs to is named for its central location among five Great Ninja Nations. What's the village called?
answer: Konohagakure (the Village Hidden in the Leaves)
choices: Konohagakure (the Village Hidden in the Leaves)
context: The five Great Ninja Villages are Konoha, Kiri, Suna, Kumo, and Iwa (Stone). Each is led by a Kage. Naruto's lifelong dream is to become the Seventh Hokage of Konoha, fulfilled at the end of Shippuden.

question: Naruto's signature jutsu, taught to him by Jiraiya, is a spinning sphere of chakra concentrated in the palm of the hand. It was originally created by Naruto's father, the Fourth Hokage. What is the technique called?
context: Minato Namikaze designed the Rasengan as an incomplete technique he hoped to combine with elemental nature transformation. Naruto eventually completes it by adding his Wind affinity to create the Rasenshuriken.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece began serialization in Weekly Shonen Jump in July 1997 and has been running continuously since. The story follows pirate captain Luffy's search for the legendary treasure left behind by the previous Pirate King. What is the treasure called?
context: Gol D. Roger, the previous Pirate King, was executed publicly 22 years before the series begins. His final words mentioned his treasure being 'in one piece' at the end of the Grand Line. The Straw Hat crew sails to find it.

question: Tite Kubo's Bleach features the Soul Society — a feudal-Japan-style afterlife realm — guarded by thirteen squads of Soul Reapers, each led by a captain. The captain-commander of the Gotei 13 at the series's start is a long-bearded, scar-faced veteran. Name him.
context: Yamamoto founded the Gotei 13 over a thousand years before the present-day story. His zanpakuto, Ryujin Jakka, is considered the strongest fire-type in the Soul Society. His handheld weapon disguises as a wooden cane.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan began serialization in September 2009 in Kodansha's Bessatsu Shonen Magazine. The anime adaptation, which became an international hit, was animated for its first three seasons by which studio?
context: Wit Studio handled Seasons 1-3. MAPPA took over for the Final Season starting in 2020 after Wit declined the heavy CGI work needed for the late-series titan scenes. Isayama originally pitched the manga to Weekly Shonen Jump and was rejected.

question: Death Note's antagonist L is later succeeded by two younger candidates from Watari's orphanage Wammy's House: a marshmallow-eating albino and a chocolate-loving blonde. Name the orphanage's two successor candidates.
context: Near (Nate River) and Mello (Mihael Keehl) split the L role after L's death — Near taking the methodical approach, Mello working with the mafia. Their rivalry drives the second half of the manga, set five years after L's death.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist features seven homunculi, each named for one of the seven deadly sins. The first homunculus encountered, who appears as a buxom woman with a tattoo on her chest, is named for which sin?
context: Arakawa structured the seven homunculi-to-sins arrangement methodically: Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Envy, Sloth, Wrath, Pride. The 2009 Brotherhood adaptation follows her manga faithfully; the 2003 anime diverged at the halfway point with its own ending.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter is famous for the author's long hiatuses due to back injuries. The series' magical aura-energy system has six categories of practitioner specialization. The protagonist Gon's specialization category is the same one as a hot-headed, brute-force style favors. What's it called?
context: The six Nen categories: Enhancement (Gon, Uvogin), Emission (Killua), Transmutation (Killua, Hisoka), Conjuration (Kurapika, Kortopi), Manipulation (Shalnark), Specialization (Chrollo). Each person has one natural category.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure has been running since 1987 across multiple generational story arcs called Parts. Part 3 — Stardust Crusaders — introduced the franchise's signature mechanic: physical manifestations of fighting-spirit power. What did Araki name them?
context: Earlier Parts 1 and 2 used 'Hamon' (Ripple) energy, derived from breathing techniques. Araki created Stands for Part 3 after watching the film Mahoroba. Each Stand has a name (Star Platinum, Magician's Red) and a tarot-card or musical-themed alias.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi (also of Hunter x Hunter) wrote Yu Yu Hakusho from 1990 to 1994 in Weekly Shonen Jump. The series' central arc — a brutal multi-day demon-realm fighting competition organized by yakuza-like demon syndicates — is named what?
context: The Dark Tournament arc spans 35 anime episodes and pits Team Urameshi against five demon teams. Toguro, the gentle-giant former human turned demon, is the arc's central antagonist. Togashi modeled the structure on real-world combat sport brackets.

question: Shuichi Shigeno began Initial D in 1995 in Weekly Young Magazine. The series is set in Gunma Prefecture, and the iconic mountain pass where Takumi races his AE86 Trueno is fictionalized from a real touge route. What real-world mountain is the pass based on?
context: Shigeno based all the Initial D mountain courses on real Gunma touge routes. Akina = Haruna, Myogi = Myogi, Akagi = Akagi, Usui = Usui, Irohazaka = Irohazaka. Real drift drivers studied the manga in the late '90s and the routes became pilgrimage sites.

question: Initial D's soundtrack popularized a high-BPM Italian dance subgenre that became inseparable from drift-racing scenes. The series' compilations were marketed by Avex Trax in Japan under what umbrella title?
context: Tracks like 'Deja Vu' by Dave Rodgers, 'Running in the 90s' by Max Coveri, and Manuel's high-speed driving anthem became Initial D signatures. Many of the artists were Italian musicians recording for the Japanese market only.

question: In the original Pokemon anime that began in April 1997, Ash Ketchum hails from a small town in the Kanto region. His mother (Delia) and the local researcher Professor Oak still live there. What is the town's name?
context: The Japanese name is Masara Town. Professor Oak's research lab gives starter Pokemon to new ten-year-old trainers. Ash arrived too late on his tenth birthday and was given the unwanted, troublesome Pikachu, who refused to enter his Poke Ball.

question: In the Pokemon anime's Indigo League arc, Ash defeats Misty for the second gym badge in Cerulean City. Her three sisters Daisy, Violet, and Lily perform as a synchronized-swimming gym group called what?
context: Misty is the youngest of four sisters and is treated as 'the runt' by them. She follows Ash on his journey partly to escape that family dynamic. Her starter Togepi hatches mid-series and becomes one of the anime's most marketable characters.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball began in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1984. The original manga's first half follows kid Goku searching for the title artifacts; gathering all seven of them lets the user make one wish. What summons the wish-granter?
answer: Calling the dragon Shenron by name with all seven balls together
choices: Calling the dragon Shenron by name with all seven balls together
Rubbing the strongest ball after midnight under the full moon
Burning a phoenix-feather offering in the seven balls' center
Chanting the secret name of King Kai over the assembled set
context: The seven Dragon Balls scatter across the planet after each wish, becoming inert orange stones for one Earth year. Bulma's invention, the Dragon Radar, lets her track them. Piccolo's Namekian variant has its own dragon, Porunga.

question: Dragon Ball Z's Saiyan arc introduced Goku's older brother — a long-haired warrior who arrives on Earth in armor demanding Goku join the Saiyan war effort. He kidnaps Goku's son Gohan to force the issue. Name him.
context: Raditz dies in the first arc but transmits a critical data point: stronger Saiyans Nappa and Vegeta are coming in one year. The arc kicks off Z's whole power-escalation cycle. His scouter introduces the franchise's signature power-level metric.

question: In Dragon Ball Z's Namek arc, Goku achieves the legendary Super Saiyan transformation for the first time when his rage explodes during a single emotional moment. What event triggers the transformation?
answer: Frieza killing Krillin in front of him
choices: Frieza killing Krillin in front of him
Vegeta dying of his wounds in the desert
Gohan being pinned by Frieza's tail
Piccolo's spirit appearing in the sky
context: Goku's Super Saiyan form on Namek is the first appearance of the iconic gold-hair/teal-eyes look. Frieza's reaction — calling it a fairy tale come true — sells the moment. The whole sequence is the franchise's most-rerun footage.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's Princess Mononoke (1997) is set in late Muromachi Japan and follows a young Emishi prince who travels west seeking the cure to a curse he received from a boar god. Name the prince.
context: Princess Mononoke was the highest-grossing film in Japan until Titanic released later that year. The Forest Spirit (the deer god Shishigami) and the wolf-raised San are the other central figures. Neil Gaiman wrote the English-dub adaptation.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's Spirited Away (2001) became the first non-English-language film to win the Best Animated Feature Oscar in 2003. The young protagonist trapped in the spirit-world bathhouse is forced to work for a witch named what?
context: Chihiro must take a new name (Sen) and forget her own to keep working. Yubaba's identical twin sister Zeniba lives at Swamp Bottom; the two characters are voiced by the same actress in both Japanese (Mari Natsuki) and English (Suzanne Pleshette).

question: Tomonori Sugihara and Takao Yoguchi adapted Aida Iro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun manga in early 2020 as a TV anime. The series is set at Kamome Academy, which is rumored to have seven famous mysterious entities. What are these entities collectively called?
context: Hanako-kun is the Seventh Mystery (of the girls' bathroom). The Seven Mysteries each represent a particular boundary or fear. The series's deeper plot involves another set of entities — the demons of Kamome — operating beneath the mysteries.

question: In Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, the loud red-haired sixth-grade exorcist apprentice from a family of professional spirit-hunters becomes Nene's classmate and a major supporting character. Name him.
context: Kou's older brother Teru is the strongest active exorcist at Kamome Academy. Kou befriends Hanako-kun despite his family's mandate to exorcise him. Kou's later friendship with the false-mystery Mitsuba is a fan-beloved subplot.

question: Hiromu Arakawa based Fullmetal Alchemist's setting Amestris loosely on an early-20th-century European nation. The state alchemists serve as 'human weapons of the State,' a phrase used by which prominent character — the Flame Alchemist?
context: Mustang served in the Ishvalan genocide as a flame alchemist and is haunted by it. His secret long-game is to take the throne and dismantle the corrupt military. Arakawa drew the Ishvalan arc to evoke real-world ethnic-cleansing scenarios.

question: In Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball, the kid Goku finds a young blue-haired girl with a strange invention on her bike — the Dragon Radar — and they begin the title hunt together. What's her name?
context: Bulma is the daughter of Dr. Brief, founder of Capsule Corp (Japan's most innovative inventor). Her name comes from the Japanese pronunciation of 'bloomers' (underwear); Toriyama named all the Briefs family after underwear. She eventually marries Vegeta.

question: In the Pokemon anime's Indigo League run, the first Pokemon Ash catches in the wild — by sheer luck on Route 1 — eventually evolves into a Butterfree that he releases in an emotional Season 1 farewell episode. What is the species he first catches?
context: Episode 3 ('Ash Catches a Pokemon') has Ash threading a Poke Ball through Pidgeotto's wings to capture the Caterpie below. The Butterfree-release episode ('Bye Bye Butterfree,' Episode 21) traumatized a generation of late-90s kids.

question: In My Hero Academia, the power All Might passes down to Deku is the eighth iteration of a quirk first stolen from a brother by another brother during the dawn of the superhuman era. The original brothers' battle established the central conflict that lasts the entire series. What are the two opposing quirks called?
answer: One For All and All For One
choices: One For All and All For One
context: All For One can steal quirks; his idealistic younger brother received One For All as a quirk-stockpiling counter. Each successor adds their strength to the next, and the brother's spirit was unwittingly attached — which is why Deku can communicate with past holders.

question: In Hajime no Ippo, Ippo's most personally significant fight is his 2000 manga title bout against the man known as 'the Naniwa Tiger' — a charismatic Osaka boxer with a brutal Smash hook that floored Ippo earlier in their first fight. The two share mutual respect by the end. Name Ippo's title-fight opponent.
context: Sendo first appeared as a heel character mocking Ippo before their first fight. He becomes the OPBF Japanese Featherweight Champion. His finishing blow, 'Smash,' is a hook from a crouched stance. Morikawa modeled Sendo loosely on real Japanese boxer Takenori Hosaka.

question: Demon Slayer's nine Hashira each master a unique Breathing Style. The Stone Hashira is a tall, blind, prayer-bead-wearing warrior universally considered the strongest among the active pillars. Tanjiro trains under him during the Hashira Training Arc. Name him.
context: Gyomei was nearly executed in his civilian life after killing demons that attacked the orphanage he tended; the law refused to believe demons existed. Stone Breathing has five forms. He fights with a flail-and-axe weapon connected by a chain, used together with bead-prayers.

question: Naruto Shippuden's first major arc introduces the Akatsuki — an S-rank criminal organization of nine missing-nin wearing red-cloud-pattern black cloaks. The arc opens with the kidnapping of which Naruto love-interest character?
context: Gaara hosts the One-Tailed Shukaku and is extracted by the Akatsuki to revive their war machine. Naruto's emotional Three-Tails-or-Eight-Tails-style berserk rage transforming sequence in the rescue arc is one of Shippuden's iconic moments. Lady Chiyo sacrifices her life to revive Gaara.

question: One Piece's first major saga ends at the island of Marineford, where the Marines plan to publicly execute Luffy's blood-sworn brother to bait the world's worst pirates into a confrontation. The brother is the son of the previous Pirate King Gol D. Roger. Name him.
answer: Portgas D. Ace, Fire Fist Ace
choices: Portgas D. Ace, Fire Fist Ace
context: Ace is the son of the executed Pirate King Gol D. Roger. He sacrifices himself blocking a magma-fist attack from Admiral Akainu meant for Luffy. The Marineford War lasted around 100 manga chapters and is considered the franchise's most catastrophic arc to that point.

question: Attack on Titan's plot pivots at the season-four mark when the geography expands to a long-suspected enemy nation across the sea. The protagonist Eren reveals that the people behind the walls aren't just survivors — they're a colonized minority of a specific ethnic group hated by the entire outside world. What are they called?
answer: Eldians, descendants of the Founding Titan's bloodline
choices: Eldians, descendants of the Founding Titan's bloodline
Subjects of Ymir, the original titan-shifter population
context: Eldians outside the walls are required to wear armbands and live in internment zones, drawing explicit parallels to 1930s Europe. Marley is the dominant continental power. The reveal recontextualizes the entire series as a story about ethnic cleansing and generational trauma.

question: Death Note's protagonist Light Yagami uses a fake identity to communicate with the world. Both L and the international media call this anonymous mass-killer by what name, which Light originally coined himself using English letters from a Japanese pronunciation of 'God of the New World'?
context: 'Kira' is a romanization of the English word 'killer' transliterated through Japanese phonetics. Light adopts it as the persona under which he claims to be God of the new world. The Kira name becomes shorthand among investigators and a cult-following emerges in-universe.

question: Fullmetal Alchemist's tragic backstory begins when Edward and Alphonse Elric try to bring their dead mother Trisha back to life through human transmutation — alchemy's ultimate taboo. The rebound costs Ed an arm and a leg; it costs Al his entire body. What do they encounter at the moment of failure that explains alchemy's source?
answer: The Gate of Truth, with the entity called Truth at its threshold
choices: The Gate of Truth, with the entity called Truth at its threshold
The Philosopher's Stone, dissolved in their mother's blood
The shadow of their father Hohenheim, watching silently
The homunculus Envy, in his serpent form, taunting them
context: Truth is a faceless white figure who personally collects the 'toll' for human-transmutation attempts. The Gate of Truth contains all knowledge of alchemy and the universe's structure. Each alchemist who sees the Gate is taking a piece of forbidden knowledge with terrible cost.

question: Hunter x Hunter's Chimera Ant arc — widely considered the series' peak — features the destruction of a small nation by ant-human hybrid monsters. The arc's climax pits the Hunter Association's chairman against the ant king Meruem in a battle ended by a smuggled-in nuclear-ish weapon called what?
answer: The Rose, a miniaturized poison bomb
choices: The Rose, a miniaturized poison bomb
The Lily, a sealed nen weapon
context: Chairman Isaac Netero detonates the Rose strapped to his chest after his last martial arts attack fails to defeat Meruem. The Rose's residual poison ultimately kills the king. Togashi spent years on this arc and it remains the most dialogue-heavy in HxH.

question: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3 follows Jotaro Kujo, his grandfather Joseph Joestar, and a multinational team on a fifty-day trek from Tokyo to Egypt to defeat their family's recurring vampire enemy before he can use a captured stand-arrow against humanity. Who is the vampire antagonist?
context: Dio appeared in Part 1 (1880s) attached to Jonathan Joestar's body. He returns in Part 3 (1989) after a century underwater. His Stand, The World, can stop time — a power that becomes the franchise's defining ability. Part 3's English dub introduced 'ZA WARUDO' to internet culture.

question: Yu Yu Hakusho's Dark Tournament arc ends with Team Urameshi facing Team Toguro in the final. The Younger Toguro reveals he was once human and chose demonic transformation. His percentage-output power-up system — going 80%, 100%, 120% — is announced openly before each escalation. What does the Younger Toguro call his maximum 120% form?
answer: His Hellfire form, the all-or-nothing terminal state
choices: His Hellfire form, the all-or-nothing terminal state
His Demon-King form, the locked-soul state
His Saint-Beast form, the holy-flame state
His Shinigami form, the death-touched state
context: Togashi's percentage-output structure later influenced Dragon Ball Super's Ultra Instinct tiers, MHA's Plus Ultra mechanics, and various tournament-arc structures. The Younger Toguro at 100% is genuinely terrifying; his 120% Hellfire form is what finally takes Yusuke seriously.

question: Shuichi Shigeno's Initial D launched in 1995 and concluded in 2013. The protagonist Takumi's Toyota Trueno AE86 — chosen by Shigeno because it was 'the worst possible choice for a serious racer in 1995' — was already a 10-year-old discontinued model when the series began. What slang nickname did the panda-colored AE86 get?
context: AE86 is the chassis code. The panda color scheme — white top, black bottom — became one of car culture's most-recognized liveries. Toyota's GT86 / Subaru BRZ revival in 2012 was directly inspired by Initial D's continuing popularity. Takumi's father Bunta drove the original.

question: In the original 1997 Pokemon anime, Ash's troubled Charmander evolves into Charmeleon and then a Charizard that famously refuses to obey him during gym battles, sleeping or burning Ash with Flamethrower at random. The arc resolves at the Indigo League where Charizard takes on which legendary trainer's Blastoise?
answer: Gary Oak's, in the league quarterfinals
choices: Gary Oak's, in the league quarterfinals
Ritchie's, in the second round preliminary
Gilbert's, in the early Indigo screening rounds
Drake's, on the Orange Islands later
context: Ash's Charizard was originally abandoned by its trainer Damian. Its obedience issue resolved when Ash refused to leave it after it was frozen by an Articuno-tier ice attack and warmed it through the night. The character became the iconic 'cool but loyal' anime starter.

question: Dragon Ball Z's Cell arc introduces an android designed by Dr. Gero to be the ultimate weapon — assembled from cells of all Z fighters and beyond. To achieve his perfect form, Cell must absorb two earlier-model androids. Which two does he hunt and absorb?
context: Androids 17 and 18 are originally human siblings (Lapis and Lazuli) who were kidnapped by Dr. Gero and converted. Cell's Perfect Form, achieved by absorbing them both, makes him sleeker, more confident, and proportionally more powerful — the arc's iconic design moment.

question: Dragon Ball Z's Buu arc reveals a vague pink demon sealed away centuries before by the previous generation of Supreme Kais. Released in the present day, Buu's fight with Goku and his sons spans the franchise's final arc. Goku's ultimate technique against Buu involves gathering energy from every living being on Earth into a single attack. What is that signature attack?
choices: The Big Bang Attack (Bigu Ban Atakku)
context: Goku first learns the Spirit Bomb from King Kai during the Saiyan arc. It uses borrowed energy and requires the donor's consent. In the Buu arc, Vegeta and others must convince Earth's population to raise their hands — a famously emotional moment as Hercule (Mr. Satan) leads the request.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's Castle in the Sky (1986) — Studio Ghibli's first official film — features two children searching for a legendary floating city. The film's score, by Joe Hisaishi, established the long Miyazaki-Hisaishi creative partnership. What is the name of the floating city?
context: Laputa is borrowed from Swift's Gulliver's Travels (the Spanish word for an inappropriate term; Miyazaki later said he didn't know the etymology). Sheeta and Pazu, the two child leads, were modeled on protagonists from older European silent films. The Hisaishi score's 'Carrying You' became an iconic Ghibli theme.

question: Demon Slayer's Mugen Train film is a direct adaptation of the Mugen Train arc from the manga (chapters 53-69). The arc concludes with the death of one of the Hashira at the hands of an Upper Moon demon — an event that traumatizes Tanjiro and the surviving squad members. Which Upper Moon kills the Flame Hashira?
context: Akaza was once a martial artist named Hakuji whose family was poisoned by yakuza. He was turned into a demon by Muzan and lost most of his human memories. Rengoku's death in the manga came as a shock to readers; Akaza later seeks rematches with strong human martial artists.

question: In My Hero Academia, the central villain organization is composed of quirk-users led by a young, dry-skinned man whose touch causes things to crumble. His mentor — All Might's arch-enemy and the original holder of the show's stolen ur-quirk — is sealed in a hi-tech prison. Name the villain leader.
context: Tomura is the grandson of Nana Shimura, the seventh One For All wielder before All Might. He was raised by All For One after his quirk Decay manifested and killed his abusive family. The character body horror — five severed-hand prosthetics covering his face — became one of MHA's most-merchandised images.

question: Hajime no Ippo's Coach Genji Kamogawa is a gruff, ex-pro fighter who runs the gym Ippo joins. His tragic backstory is revealed in flashback: as a young boxer, he had a long-standing rivalry with a kindred-spirit American GI he met during the postwar occupation of Japan. What was the GI's name?
answer: Ralph Anderson, called 'Smith' in the dub
choices: Ralph Anderson, called 'Smith' in the dub
Mike Tyson, in the GI's dub
Jack Dempsey Jr., a fictional descendant
Billy Conn, the GI's middleweight rival
context: Kamogawa and Smith fought a brutal exhibition that ended with Kamogawa's pinky finger badly damaged. The arc emphasizes that Coach Kamogawa's choice to retire and become a trainer was driven by guilt over an earlier opponent he killed in the ring during the same era.

question: In Demon Slayer, the breathing techniques originally derive from a single ancient style mastered by the legendary first-known demon slayer. The four 'sun-derived' styles practiced by current Hashira (Water, Flame, Thunder, Stone, Wind) are all branches from this original technique. What is the original breathing style called?
context: Yoriichi Tsugikuni, the original swordsman, invented Sun Breathing and was the only person ever to develop the Demon Slayer Mark naturally. Tanjiro's family preserved the original Sun Breathing as a religious dance called Hinokami Kagura, taught from father to son in secret.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball was loosely inspired by the classical Chinese novel Journey to the West, with kid Goku as a stand-in for the Monkey King Sun Wukong. Like Sun Wukong, Goku originally had a monkey tail — which transformed under the full moon into what?
answer: A giant ape called the Oozaru, hundreds of feet tall
choices: A giant ape called the Oozaru, hundreds of feet tall
A giant flame-breathing tiger called the Konjishi
A dragon-headed warrior called the Ryusenjin
context: Saiyans transform into Oozaru under any moon's reflected sunlight, increasing their power roughly tenfold but losing most rational control. Vegeta's tail is also cut off; eventually almost all Saiyans on Earth lose their tails. The Great Ape transformation appears one last time in DBZ Cell arc through Cell Junior.

question: In Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, the seven school mysteries each represent a specific supernatural rumor. The third mystery is a literal mirror that switches souls between people who look into it. The mystery's name in Japanese is 'Misaki Stairs' — what dramatic event from the school's history caused its existence?
answer: A schoolgirl named Misaki was bullied to suicide on the back staircase decades ago
choices: A schoolgirl named Misaki was bullied to suicide on the back staircase decades ago
A teacher named Misaki was murdered by students during the war years
A young art teacher named Misaki disappeared mid-class and was never found
A student named Misaki accidentally died in a chemistry-lab fire
context: The first three mysteries are introduced relatively quickly in the manga. Misaki Stairs becomes important in a body-swap arc involving Nene and a classmate. Each of the Seven Mysteries has a specific 'territory' on the school grounds that bounds its power.

question: Naruto Shippuden's antagonist for the main arcs is the masked man calling himself Tobi, later revealed as the long-presumed-dead teammate of Kakashi from the Third Ninja War. The character was traumatized after watching his crush Rin die. What is his actual name?
context: Obito was crushed by a boulder during a mission as a child, dying — Kakashi thought — and giving him his left Sharingan eye. Madara Uchiha actually preserved his body, healed him, and trained him over decades. The reveal that Obito was Tobi recontextualizes the entire Shippuden plot.

question: Tite Kubo's Bleach is structured around four major arcs. The third arc, the longest in the series, follows Ichigo and friends rescuing a captured comrade from execution in the Soul Society — which involves storming the central building of the Gotei 13's seat of government. What is that central tower called?
answer: Senzaikyu, the Tower of Penitence atop Sokyoku Hill
choices: Senzaikyu, the Tower of Penitence atop Sokyoku Hill
Seireitei Citadel and the Sealed Inner Vault
The Kuchiki Manor and Captain's Senate Hall
The Royal Realm of the Soul King's Palace
context: The Soul Society arc spans about 60 chapters and 40-plus anime episodes. The arc reveals Captain Aizen's long con — he was orchestrating the entire crisis to forge a god-tier item called the Hogyoku. The execution sequence remains one of Bleach's most-discussed cliffhangers.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece introduced the Devil Fruit-power system in Chapter 1. The fruits come in three categories, each conferring a different style of ability — Paramecia (transformative-static), Zoan (animal-form), and the rarest and most powerful third category. What is the third Devil Fruit category called?
context: Logia users can transform their bodies into and control an element — fire (Ace), magma (Akainu), light (Kizaru), darkness (Blackbeard). They're functionally immune to most physical attacks unless the opponent has Armament Haki or Sea-Prism Stone. Only a few dozen are known by the series' early arcs.

question: Death Note's character L is famous for an unconventional crouched-sitting posture and constant sugar consumption. He cracks all major cases under multiple alias names. His real name — known only to a handful of people, since revealing it would let any Death Note holder kill him — is what?
context: L is the world's top three detectives all rolled into one anonymous identity. Watari (Quillsh Wammy) is his handler and the founder of Wammy's House orphanage that produces his successor candidates. Light learns L's real name in the manga only at the very moment L is dying.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist features the homunculus Father, the antagonist whose plan is to consume an entire country's worth of human souls in a single transmutation circle drawn across the national borders. The country, modeled on early-20th-century Germany, is named what?
context: The seven homunculi are each made from Father's own discarded sins. Father plans to absorb God (the entity called Truth) using Amestris's population as living sacrifices. The bordering nations Aerugo, Drachma, Creta, and the eastern Xing form the surrounding political landscape.

question: Tomonori Sugihara's anime adaptation of Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun heavily emphasized chalk-on-blackboard-style transitions and a distinctive watercolor color palette. The opening theme song became an instant fan favorite. What was the opening theme called?
choices: Mizu no Yume by Bump of Chicken
context: The Jibaku Shounen Band is a fictional in-universe band assembled for the anime's marketing campaign with voice actors as members. The 'No.7' title references Hanako as the seventh mystery. The anime aired in early 2020 and was animated by Lerche.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball Z's Saiyan arc opens with the death of Goku at the hands of his brother Raditz. Goku willingly holds Raditz still while his rival fires a beam through both of them. The rival sacrificing himself in the same attack is a longtime enemy of Goku turned reluctant ally. Name him.
context: Piccolo's Special Beam Cannon (Makankosappo) is the only technique strong enough to pierce Raditz's armor in that scene. Both Goku and Raditz die. Piccolo's redemption arc — from Demon King's son to mentor of Goku's son Gohan — is one of DBZ's most beloved character developments.

question: In My Hero Academia, the Sports Festival in Season 2 ends with a final tournament that crowns one of Class 1-A as the top first-year combatant of UA High. The festival's iconic final fight between two ice-and-fire-quirked students became the franchise's first 'classic' battle. Who won the tournament?
answer: Katsuki Bakugo, who was strapped to a pillar for the medal ceremony
choices: Katsuki Bakugo, who was strapped to a pillar for the medal ceremony
Shoto Todoroki, who refused to use his fire side until the final
Izuku Midoriya, who broke both his arms beating Shinso
Tenya Iida, who used his engine-quirk Recipro Burst to clinch it
context: The festival ran from chapters 23 to 44 of the manga. Bakugo's refusal to accept his championship gracefully — he wanted to fight Todoroki at full power — became one of the series' character-defining beats. The medal-podium pillar gag became fan meme material.

question: Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia features a hero called Eraserhead — a stoic, sleep-deprived underground hero whose quirk lets him cancel another person's quirk just by looking at them. He's the homeroom teacher of Class 1-A and gets the franchise's most badass slow-pan introduction in the USJ Attack arc. His civilian name reveals a Japanese pun on what kind of object?
answer: His name Shota Aizawa contains 'aizawa' (a play on 'eraser' (keshigomu) and his quirk's nature)
choices: His name Shota Aizawa contains 'aizawa' (a play on 'eraser' (keshigomu) and his quirk's nature)
His name Shoto Aizawa intentionally rhymes with his Boku no Hero predecessor
His name Shota Aizawa was a pre-existing villain from My Hero Academia: Vigilantes
His name Shota Aizawa shares kanji with 'eraser-headed Buddhist saint'
context: Eraserhead's quirk, Erasure, only works while he keeps eye contact and doesn't blink. The signature scarf he wears is a special capture weapon made of stiffened steel-wire-and-cloth. His pessimistic line 'You'd better all be ready to take this seriously' became one of MHA's most-quoted moments.

question: Hajime no Ippo's most famous training sequence is the legendary 'beach training' arc, where Coach Kamogawa drags Ippo and Takamura to a coastal village to push their conditioning beyond human limits. Takamura's regimen included carrying a massive piece of equipment for hours on end across the sand. What piece of equipment did Takamura carry through his beach training?
answer: A horsedrawn carriage tire used for sled-pull resistance training
choices: A horsedrawn carriage tire used for sled-pull resistance training
A boulder strapped to his back called the Iwa-no-Kokuhaku stone
A pair of fishing nets weighed down by lead sinkers in each hand
A pull-cart of cement bags totaling 80 kilograms across the beach
context: Takamura's beach training is one of Hajime no Ippo's most-replicated sequences in shonen sports manga. The visual of him sprinting up sand dunes with the massive tire became an anime staple. Coach Kamogawa's actual training methods were partly modeled on the brutal Toko Boxing Gym regimen in 1950s Tokyo.

question: Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer concluded its manga run in May 2020 with a final battle against Muzan that spans over 80 chapters. The climax of the final fight features Tanjiro temporarily becoming the strongest demon ever — having been bitten by the dying Muzan and inheriting his blood. The arc resolves with one of Tanjiro's friends slashing through a tearfully-shouted plea to save him. Who reaches him in time?
answer: His sister Nezuko, who reverses his demon transformation through her own restored humanity
choices: His sister Nezuko, who reverses his demon transformation through her own restored humanity
His mentor Giyu Tomioka, with Lady Tamayo's antidote arrow shot through the demon mark
His friend Zenitsu, with the Seventh Form of Thunder Breathing newly mastered
His master Sakonji Urokodaki, who returns from retirement for the final battle
context: The Tanjiro-as-demon sequence is one of the manga's most-debated reveals. Nezuko's restored humanity (achieved earlier through the Lady Tamayo medicine and her own willpower) is what gives her the spiritual force to reach her brother. Gotouge gave the manga a 23-chapter epilogue set in modern-day Tokyo with reincarnated descendants of the cast.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto Shippuden runs for around 500 episodes covering the Fourth Great Ninja War — an alliance of all five Hidden Villages against the resurrected ninja army of the Akatsuki and an ancient goddess. The war arc spans about 200 episodes alone (a notoriously high filler rate). The 'final villain' the alliance fights at the war's conclusion is a primordial being from another dimension named what?
answer: Kaguya Otsutsuki, the original chakra-tree progenitor
choices: Kaguya Otsutsuki, the original chakra-tree progenitor
Hagoromo Otsutsuki, the sage of the six paths
context: Kaguya was a late addition to the manga's lore — introduced in the final 30 chapters — and many fans found her arc rushed. She's the mother of the sage Hagoromo and a being who ate the chakra fruit from the Divine Tree millennia before the series's present day. Her introduction recontextualized Madara and Obito as pawns.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece introduces a power system in the early arcs called Haki — willpower-as-aura-energy — that becomes the high-level combat metric of the latter series. There are three confirmed types: Armament (defensive), Observation (perceptive), and the rarest type that only one in a million can use. What is the rare third type called?
answer: Conqueror's Haki (Haoshoku Haki / Color of the King)
choices: Conqueror's Haki (Haoshoku Haki / Color of the King)
Emperor's Haki (Yonkō Haki / Color of the Throne)
Pirate-King's Haki (Kaizoku Ō Haki / Color of the Crown)
Dragon's Haki (Ryūou Haki / Color of the World)
context: Conqueror's Haki is innate — it cannot be trained, only awakened. Holders can knock out weaker beings just by exerting it. Notable users: Luffy, Shanks, Whitebeard, Roger, Big Mom, Kaido. The Wano arc revealed Conqueror's can be coated on weapons or strikes at the most advanced levels.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan revealed its central mystery across the four seasons: the giant titans that destroyed humanity decades ago aren't mindless monsters — they're transformed humans of a specific ethnicity, descended from an ancient queen. The Nine Titan-shifter powers can be inherited by eating their previous holder. The Founding Titan, the most powerful, can only be commanded by someone with royal blood. What ancient queen founded the Eldian lineage that holds the Titan power?
answer: Ymir Fritz, the slave-girl who made a pact with the Devil of All Earth
choices: Ymir Fritz, the slave-girl who made a pact with the Devil of All Earth
Karl Fritz, the 145th Eldian king who erected the walls
Frieda Reiss, the Reiss-family Founding Titan holder before Grisha
Historia Reiss, the rightful queen during the Survey Corps's coup
context: Ymir Fritz's bargain with the Devil of All Earth gave the Eldians their titan powers 2,000 years before the present. After her death, her body was split among her three daughters and the lineage became hereditary. The reveal that the Founding Titan is essentially God-tier is the Season 3 / 4 pivot of the entire series.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has an iconic chapter where L confronts Light directly for the first time at the university entrance ceremony, both having been declared the top scorer. The two meet under fake names and the meeting establishes the central cat-and-mouse rivalry. What university hosts the meeting?
answer: To-Oh University, fictional Tokyo Imperial-style elite institution
choices: To-Oh University, fictional Tokyo Imperial-style elite institution
Tokyo University (Todai), the real-world institution Light secretly attends
Kanto Hogan University, the elite criminology-program school
Daikoku University, the fictional analogue to Kyoto Imperial
context: Light entered To-Oh under his own name; L appeared as the alias 'Hideki Ryuga' (sharing a name with a real Japanese pop star, a deliberate Ohba joke). The entrance ceremony scene where L whispers 'I am L' to Light became one of the manga's most-iconic two-page spreads.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist concluded its manga run in 2010 with the climactic final battle against Father, the homunculus who'd been planning to consume the souls of all of Amestris in a nationwide transmutation circle. The plan exploited a series of carefully-positioned events across the entire country's history, each generating a mass-casualty 'crimson stone' as a tool for the final ritual. The original Ishvalan war was deliberately engineered by Father for this exact purpose. The military's high-ranking insider who orchestrated his side of the plan is named what?
answer: King Bradley, the Fuhrer Pride homunculus
choices: King Bradley, the Fuhrer Pride homunculus
General Hakuro, the Briggs Mountain commander
General Grumman, Roy Mustang's secret backer
General Olivier Armstrong, the Briggs Northern Front
context: Bradley was Father's homunculus seventh sin, Pride — an experiment that began with a human body rather than alchemical creation. His Ultimate Eye lets him predict any opponent's moves. The reveal that Amestris's entire history was a multi-century setup orchestrated by Father is the manga's largest single plot twist.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter Chimera Ant arc features a 30-day siege of a small nation called the Republic of East Gorteau by an army of ant-human hybrids. The ant king Meruem is born during the siege. The Hunter Association's Chairman Netero — the series' established 'strongest human' — challenges Meruem to a one-on-one fight that ends with Netero detonating a poison bomb hidden in his chest cavity. What's the bomb called?
answer: The Miniature Rose, a nuclear-yield poison weapon stolen from a national arsenal
choices: The Miniature Rose, a nuclear-yield poison weapon stolen from a national arsenal
The Lotus Sutra, an ancient sealing scroll from the Heaven's Arena
The Cherry Bomb, a Black-Whale-Association explosive prototype
The Iris Trial, an antiquity-class transmutation curse from Yorknew
context: Togashi modeled the Miniature Rose loosely on real nuclear-weapon designs. The bomb does kill Meruem eventually — but only after Meruem reconnects with the blind human girl Komugi he's befriended. Their final shared game of Gungi (the made-up board game) is one of HxH's most-quoted scenes.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 4 — Diamond is Unbreakable — is set in 1999 in a small Japanese town called Morioh-cho. The arc's antagonist is a quiet office worker who collects severed-hand mementos of women he murders. His Stand grants him the ability to detonate any object he touches. Araki cited a real-world Japanese murderer as partial inspiration. What is the antagonist's name?
answer: Yoshikage Kira, an unassuming middle-aged man
choices: Yoshikage Kira, an unassuming middle-aged man
Akira Otoishi, the electric-rocker Stand user
Keicho Nijimura, the elder Nijimura brother
Anjuro Katagiri, the convict turned water Stand user
context: Kira's Stand, Killer Queen, can charge an object as a bomb and detonate it remotely. His desire is for a 'quiet life' free of being noticed. Araki's design choice — a normal-looking salaryman as the villain — was a deliberate subversion of JoJo's typically flamboyant antagonists. The 'Yoshikage Kira self-introduction' speech became internet-meme material.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Yu Yu Hakusho concluded its run in 1994 after Togashi developed back problems that forced an abrupt ending. The final arc — Three Kings — was severely truncated compared to the original plan. The story's epilogue jumps three years and shows the cast working at a humble noodle shop. Who runs this shop?
answer: Yusuke's grandfather Atsuko, alongside his now-adult girlfriend Keiko
choices: Yusuke's grandfather Atsuko, alongside his now-adult girlfriend Keiko
Genkai, the master who trained Yusuke before her death and revival
Kuwabara's older sister Shizuru, who ran a hostess club through the series
Yusuke himself, with Botan and Hiei occasionally visiting
context: Atsuko is actually Yusuke's mother (a notable name confusion in some translations). Yusuke's noodle-shop ending is unusually downbeat for a shonen finale — Togashi reportedly cited his exhaustion with the format. The Yu Yu Hakusho ending influenced Togashi's approach to Hunter x Hunter's open-ended structure.

question: Shuichi Shigeno's Initial D concluded its manga run in July 2013, after about 18 years of serialization. Takumi's final race against the white-jersey'd MR-2-turbo-driving Project D rival Shinji Inui ended the series with a tone of bittersweet ambiguity rather than victory. Where was the final race held?
answer: Mt. Akagi, in Project D's hometown-circuit conclusion
choices: Mt. Akagi, in Project D's hometown-circuit conclusion
Mt. Akina, the original training mountain returning for the finale
Mt. Haruna, the local touge of the Real Akina geography
Mt. Tsumagoi, an unfamiliar northern course neutral to both teams
context: Project D is the third-generation racing team Takumi and Keisuke Takahashi join in the manga's later arcs. Shinji is the AE86's rival driver — younger, naturally talented, and clearly modeled as a 'mirror' Takumi figure. The MF Ghost manga (2017-) continues the Initial D universe with a new protagonist and Takumi as a senior figure.

question: Studio Ghibli's Princess Mononoke (1997) featured a famously complex production. The animation team hand-drew over 144,000 frames at Studio Ghibli's Tokyo studios, with Miyazaki personally retouching about 80,000 of them. The film's English dub featured Claire Danes as San and Billy Crudup as Ashitaka, alongside a famous cast member voicing the demon-cursed boar god in the opening sequence. Who played that role?
answer: Keith David, the actor known for his deep growling voice work
choices: Keith David, the actor known for his deep growling voice work
Liam Neeson, fresh off his Schindler's List performance
Patrick Stewart, in a brief opening-narration cameo
Gillian Anderson, also voicing Moro the wolf goddess
context: Neil Gaiman wrote the English dub script, working closely with Miyazaki's exacting standards. Studio Ghibli's Miramax distribution deal famously required a 'no cuts' clause — Harvey Weinstein wanted to trim Mononoke; Miyazaki sent him a katana with 'No Cuts' inscribed on it. Gillian Anderson did voice the wolf goddess Moro.

question: Aida Iro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun reveals across its arcs that Hanako-kun and his twin brother Tsukasa were both 13 when they died — and Hanako (then Amane Yugi) killed his own twin before being killed himself. This twin-tragedy backstory is one of the manga's most-debated plot points. The boys' violin-playing twin family lived in what kind of neighborhood?
answer: A traditional middle-class working-family neighborhood with their seamstress mother absent often
choices: A traditional middle-class working-family neighborhood with their seamstress mother absent often
A wealthy uptown district where their politician father had been promoted recently
An impoverished urban ward where their orphaned grandmother raised them alone
A rural farming village where their elderly grandfather served as the local priest
context: The Amane-and-Tsukasa backstory is revealed across multiple flashback arcs in the manga. The 'why did Amane kill his twin' mystery is central to the deeper plot. Aida Iro's clear, painterly art style and gentle horror aesthetic earned the series significant adult readership beyond the typical shonen demographic.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball franchise's Z continuation aired from 1989 to 1996 on Fuji TV. The series ran into significant production challenges with the original manga — Toriyama drew the manga concurrently with the anime's airing, and the anime often outpaced his pages, leading to substantial filler. The infamous 'Frieza vs Goku' final battle on Namek was supposedly five minutes of in-story time, but spanned how many episodes of the anime?
answer: Roughly 19 episodes, spread across about half a year of weekly broadcast
choices: Roughly 19 episodes, spread across about half a year of weekly broadcast
Roughly 12 episodes, the standard 'major-arc' length of late-80s anime
Roughly 30 episodes, the most-padded fight in DBZ history
Roughly 7 episodes, surprisingly faithful to the manga's pace
context: The 'five minutes that lasted half a year' became a meme even at the time. The reason: Namek's planet-destruction countdown was set at five minutes of real time, which the anime stretched to allow Toriyama to keep up with his manga pace. The actual planet-destruction shockwave was eventually filmed to dramatic effect.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball GT (1996-1997) was an anime-only continuation that ran for one year after the manga ended. The series was poorly received by hardcore fans for its tonal departure, but produced one universally-praised technical innovation: Goku achieves a transformation never seen in the manga, with red fur all over his body and a regrown monkey tail. What is the transformation called?
context: Super Saiyan 4 was designed by Tadayoshi Yamamuro, Dragon Ball's chief animation director. The form bypasses the gold-haired SSJ aesthetic for red fur and a Mohawk-style mane, returning to the Saiyans' Great Ape-tied roots. The form is non-canonical to Toriyama's later Dragon Ball Super continuity but remains beloved.

question: Tite Kubo's Bleach concluded its manga run in August 2016 after 686 chapters, with the final arc — the Thousand-Year Blood War — depicting the Soul Society's final war against an ancient race of Hollow-related humans called the Quincy. The Quincy King is an immortal being who's been waiting in a frozen state for centuries. What is his name?
choices: Aizen Sosuke, the original master deceiver
Kisuke Urahara, in his Quincy form revealed
context: Yhwach is the father of the Quincy race and a son of the Soul King himself. His power, 'The Almighty,' lets him see and rewrite the future. The Thousand-Year Blood War arc was animated in three cours from 2022 to 2024 — almost a decade after the manga concluded — by Studio Pierrot.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece reached a major narrative milestone in the Wano Country arc (2018-2022, manga chapters 909-1057), which concluded the long-running 'Pirates vs. Yonko' subplot by defeating two of the Four Emperors of the New World simultaneously. The arc also revealed the true name of Luffy's Devil Fruit, which had been called 'Gum-Gum Fruit' since chapter one but was actually a Mythical Zoan. What is the Fruit's true name?
answer: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika (the Human-Human Fruit, the Sun God form)

The reveal explains many of the franchise's earlier-arc mysteries (Joy Boy, the Will of D., the Void Century). Luffy's Gear 5 transformation — pure white with cartoonish rubber-physics absurdity — was the most-shared anime moment of 2023.

question: Aida Iro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun was animated by Lerche in early 2020 with director Masaomi Ando. The opening sequence used a distinctive paper-doll-cutout art style. The animation's color palette was an unusual choice for a horror-leaning supernatural series — heavy on what specific color tone?
answer: Soft pastel watercolors with chalk-blackboard accents

Stark monochrome with neon-light highlight accents
Bright saturation with high-contrast comic-book inks
context: The series' distinctive look — chalk transitions, watercolor backgrounds, paper-cutout intro — set it apart from typical 2020s anime aesthetics. The opening sequence inspired countless TikTok and AMV recreations. Aida Iro's original manga art style is even more delicate; the anime adapted it with admirable fidelity.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto Shippuden arc 'Pain's Assault' (episodes 152-175) features the Akatsuki member Pain leveling the entire Hidden Leaf Village in a single attack. Pain's true identity is a young Akatsuki-founder named Nagato, who controls six bodies remotely as his 'Six Paths.' answer: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage and Pervy Sage from Naruto's backstory

Jiraiya's death at Pain's hands in his investigative encounter is one of Shippuden's most devastating arcs. The reveal that Pain was Jiraiya's pupil mirrors Naruto's relationship with Jiraiya himself.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure has employed musical-name references for character and Stand names since Part 1 (1987). The infamous 'David Production anime curse' is the legal-clearance problem Araki's nomenclature creates. The Stand for Brando in Part 3 — 'The World' — is a reference to which musical entity?

The 1969 Beatles album cut 'Across the Universe' (extended track name)

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter introduced the assassination-family of Killua Zoldyck — Gon's best friend and the franchise's iconic deuteragonist. question: The original 1997 Pokemon anime's first season — known as the Indigo League — ran for 82 episodes, ending with Ash's appearance at the title League. Ash placed in the Top 16 in the league after a strong run was derailed by his Charizard's refusal to obey during a critical match. Which trainer beat Ash in that decisive Indigo League round?
answer: Ritchie, an Ash lookalike trainer with a Pikachu nicknamed Sparky

context: Ritchie's appearance as a 'mirror Ash' character — same enthusiasm, same Pikachu, slightly more responsible — was a deliberate narrative beat. The Indigo League finale's lesson: Ash isn't ready to be a Pokemon Master yet. Ritchie himself loses in the next round, suggesting the same lesson applies broadly. The animator Masamitsu Hidaka cited the loss as character-defining.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball Z's Cell Saga concluded with the Cell Games — a martial-arts tournament Cell organizes to announce his perfect form to humanity. Goku, having trained alongside his son Gohan in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber, surprises everyone by stepping out of the final fight and pushing Gohan forward. Why does Goku withdraw?
answer: Goku has determined Gohan has greater untapped potential and a hidden form Cell hasn't seen

Goku has been Saiyan-cursed by Vegeta's secret bargain and cannot win the fight
context: Gohan goes Super Saiyan 2 for the first time in the Cell Games after Cell crushes Android 16's last words. The transformation, animated by Mitsuo Hashimoto, became one of DBZ's most iconic moments. Gohan's Cell-decimating Kamehameha was set up by Goku from the other side; the father-son combo move is one of the franchise's most emotional sequences.

question: Studio Ghibli's Howl's Moving Castle (2004) was directed by Hayao Miyazaki and based on the 1986 Diana Wynne Jones novel. The film's English dub featured a notable A-list cast and a famously elegant fire-demon character voiced by what well-known American comedian?

Calcifer is the fire-demon that powers Howl's moving castle through a contract that's secretly bound to Howl's heart. Disney distributed the dub through Miramax until that contract ended.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball franchise's recurring 'Hyperbolic Time Chamber' is a pocket dimension where one Earth-day equals one full year of training. The chamber sits inside Kami's Lookout, the floating palace at the top of Korin Tower. The chamber has specific entry restrictions: only two trainees at a time, and lifetime use limited per individual. What is the lifetime entry limit?

The chamber's environment — 50x Earth gravity, harsh temperature extremes, no horizon — makes survival difficult. question: In Naruto Shippuden, the major character death that traumatized the fanbase most in the war arc was a sage-cloaked, fox-summoning ninja master killed by Pain in his investigative encounter. The death scene featured the master writing his final findings on his opponent's back in coded text as his last act. Name the master.
answer: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage of Mt. Myoboku
choices: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage of Mt. Myoboku

Pain — actually his student Nagato's six-corpse-puppet — defeated him in close combat using a body that hadn't been revealed. Jiraiya's death is widely cited as one of shonen's most-emotional sequences. His sacrifice cracks the Pain mystery for Konoha.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has an iconic chapter where Light realizes L is in the same room as him for the first time. Obata's drawing style on this sequence — close-ups of eyes, the ball, the racket — became defining for the manga's psychological-thriller register. The eventual face-to-face came at the To-Oh entrance ceremony.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece's Marineford War arc featured the death of the World's Strongest Man Edward Newgate — alias Whitebeard — during his attempt to rescue Luffy's brother Ace from public execution. Whitebeard's final death pose was a famously dramatic standing-corpse moment with both arms folded. His final words named his successor and addressed Blackbeard. He confessed that the Ancient Weapons were all held by Eldian descendants of an erased kingdom

His final words — 'The One Piece does exist!' — were the single biggest plot confirmation in over a decade of the manga. Blackbeard's subsequent body-double-Devil-Fruit acquisition created a one-of-a-kind exception to the franchise's power rules. Marco the Phoenix took over leadership of Whitebeard's remnants.

question: Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia features a recurring battle structure involving 'Pillar' heroes, the franchise's tier above standard Pro Heroes. The series's number-two hero — Endeavor — is the Pillar hero who covers western Japan. His son Shoto Todoroki famously refused to use the inherited fire-side of his quirk for years. What pulled Shoto out of that refusal?
answer: Deku's heart-to-heart with him during their Sports Festival fight

His mother Rei's hospital recovery and explicit forgiveness offered
Endeavor's near-death battle against the high-end Nomu years later

context: The Sports Festival arc semi-final fight between Deku and Todoroki is one of MHA's defining episodes. Deku — bleeding, broken, and using One For All at minimum percent — convinced Todoroki that his fire was 'his own, not his father's.' The scene cemented Horikoshi's reputation for combining shonen fights with character development. Todoroki's reconciliation with his family unfolds over the manga's last 100 chapters.

question: Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia features Class 1-A's homeroom teacher Eraserhead, whose civilian face was hidden behind long black hair and bandages for most of his first appearances. The signature scarf he wraps around his neck is actually a specific kind of capture weapon made from a stiffened steel wire and cloth blend. Horikoshi has noted in interviews that the scarf's design was inspired by a specific real-world Japanese martial-arts tool — a flexible weapon used by samurai's wives to capture intruders in their absence. What is the real-world tool called?
answer: The kusarigamoke, a weighted chain-and-sash combination used in traditional ninjutsu

The kogarashi, a ceremonial pole-arm sash worn by the wives of Heian samurai
The senshibo, a folded-cloth disguise used by Edo-era women shogunate spies

The 'samurai's wife' framing — a protector character who watches the household when men are away — fits Eraserhead's underground-hero personality. Horikoshi also studied the legendary onna-bugeisha warrior women's traditional weapon-craft for inspiration.

question: Hajime no Ippo's most famous training-arc image — the AC-current-jump-rope-with-pull-up-bar combination Takamura performs in his beach training — was reportedly modeled after a real-world strength regimen of a 1980s Japanese kickboxer. Morikawa Jouji visited multiple gyms researching the manga in the late 1980s. The actual gym whose roster of fighters Morikawa cited most heavily as his Kamogawa Boxing Gym template was located where?
answer: Sotomei-Yotsuya Boxing Gym in Tokyo, run by retired champion Eiji Sakurai during the 1980s

Nagoya Kamogawa Gym, the actual real-world namesake of the manga's gym name

He interviewed dozens of active and retired professional boxers, trained at multiple gyms personally, and consulted on every fight choreography with real coaches. The Sotomei-Yotsuya influence is documented in his published author's notes. Coach Kamogawa was loosely modeled on multiple real-life gym owners, with Sakurai-style discipline blended in.

question: Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer was animated by Ufotable studio, who developed a distinctive digital-effects technique to handle the breathing-style attacks visually. Each breathing style — Water, Flame, Thunder — has its own signature color palette and animation feel. The water-style attacks famously look like they're being rendered as actual flowing water rather than illustrated effects. What 3D-to-2D production technique did Ufotable use for these sequences?

The Mugen Train film's effect-animation work won multiple Japanese animation awards. The 'digital chiaroscuro' technique was originally developed for their Fate/Zero adaptation in 2011.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga used a recurring narrative device — chakra-mark sealing — that has roots in real Japanese folk-religious tradition. The 'Dragon Sealing Method' Jiraiya uses to bind the Nine-Tailed Fox into baby Naruto draws from a real-world ritualistic talisman class associated with which Shinto temple complex?
answer: Mount Koya's esoteric Buddhist-Shinto syncretic tradition, with mountain-ascetic Tendai influences

The 'Five Element' chakra system (Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Lightning) corresponds to the Godai cosmology shared between Shinto and Buddhist traditions. The Jinchuriki concept — humans imprisoning gods — has loose parallels to real-world Inari fox-spirit lore.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece set a Guinness World Record in 2022 for the most copies published of a single comic book series by an individual author — over 516 million copies worldwide. The previous record-holder for most-published-by-single-author was Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball. The series has been the best-selling manga of every single year from 2008 through the present.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan reached its serialization conclusion in April 2021 after 139 chapters across 12 years. The final chapter's title was a specific Japanese phrase meaning 'Toward the Tree on That Hill' — a callback to the manga's opening dream-sequence in chapter one. The Last Boy in the World

The fan reaction to the actual final chapter was mixed — some celebrated the bookended structure, others felt the ending was rushed. The 4-page extended ending released several months later softened the controversy.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has an iconic recurring object: the Death Note itself, with a black leather cover and English-language inscription. The notebook's rules — 'The human whose name is written in this notebook shall die' — are introduced in the cold open of chapter one. Obata's drawing of the actual physical notebook went through several design iterations. The final notebook design was based on what specific real-world object Ohba and Obata used as reference?

The English-language 'Death Note' lettering on the cover became one of the manga's most iconic visual elements. The 2017 Netflix adaptation's prop notebook was also custom-made to Obata's design.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist features Edward Elric's signature transmutation circle — a hand-clapping fast-circle technique he developed after seeing the Gate of Truth. The hand-clap is a faster alternative to drawing a circle on the ground or having one tattooed on the palms. His prosthetic automail arm contained a built-in transmutation array invented by Winry

Other circle-less alchemists include Alphonse (also paid the toll for the failed transmutation), Izumi Curtis (paid for losing her ability to bear children), and the homunculus Father (who is essentially a transmutation circle made flesh). The 'hand-clap' technique became one of the manga's most-imitated visual signatures.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter has been famous for the author's frequent hiatuses — Togashi's chronic back pain has interrupted serialization repeatedly since 1998. The longest single continuous hiatus in the manga's run was a multi-year break that lasted from 2018 to 2022. During that hiatus, Shueisha continued to publish status updates from Togashi on his Twitter account documenting his slow page-by-page progress. Togashi's published explanations cite a herniated disc and chronic lower-back problems that prevent him from drawing at a manga-rate page schedule. His wife Naoko Takeuchi (creator of Sailor Moon) has reportedly assisted with some assistance-tasks during his recovery.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure has gone through 9 Parts over its 38-year run. Araki's distinctive art style — exaggerated muscle anatomy, theatrical posing, fashion-magazine influences — has evolved dramatically across the Parts. Araki himself appears in the manga periodically as a self-portrait character drawn in his typical Italian-fashion-art style. His 2018 art exhibition at the Louvre paired his work with Renaissance pieces.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Yu Yu Hakusho concluded in 1994 with the Three Kings arc — a shortened version of his original plan. Togashi had originally pitched Yu Yu Hakusho to Weekly Shonen Jump as a much darker, more political series with a different protagonist concept than the eventual Yusuke.
